newsitem.title: INDIA: India BPCL issue attracts big investors.
newsitem.headline: India BPCL issue attracts big investors.

text.p: Indian refining firm Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd's (BPCL) 4.12 billion rupee equity issue has received a strong response from large investors, lead manager ICICI Securities and Finance Co (I-Sec) said on Friday.
An I-Sec spokesman told Reuters the 20 percent component for domestic mutual funds and financial institutions had already been placed.
A further 15 percent reserved for foreign institutional investors (FIIs) had also been placed, the spokesman said.
The public issue is scheduled to open in the last week of October.
"The issue is meeting with an extremely good response especially from long-term institutional investors," he said.

The issue would reduce the government's holding in BPCL to 60.18 percent from 66.2 percent. Funds received will be used to partly finance BPCL's capital expenditure of 57.2 billion rupees upto the year 1999/2000.
BPCL is one of India's three leading refiners with a market share of 20.3 percent during 1995/96 (April-March). Its Bombay refinery refines 7.2 million tonnes of crude annually.
